# Viruses

> *What is a virus, and why does it depend completely on a living cell?*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
This chapter will follow the same template as the *Gram-positive cocci* chapter. The outline below
shows what it will cover.
:::

**The group in one sentence:** Genetic material in a protein coat, sometimes wrapped in a lipid
envelope, that can only copy itself inside a living cell.

**How members differ (the sorting key):** DNA or RNA genome; whether the genome can be read
directly; enveloped or naked.

**Main organisms (full profile cards):** influenza virus (enveloped, segmented RNA genome that
reshuffles), dengue virus (mosquito-borne, Singapore relevance), the enteroviruses of hand, foot and
mouth disease (naked, survive hand sanitiser), HIV (copies its RNA into DNA).

**Supporting organisms (one table row each):** hepatitis B virus, herpesviruses (latency), human
papillomavirus, SARS-CoV-2, measles virus.

**Later in the course:** respiratory, liver, sexually transmitted and childhood infections in the organ
blocks; vaccines in immunology; antiviral drugs in pharmacology.
